study_identification.title: Regional, circuit and network heterogeneity of brain abnormalities in psychiatric disorders

study_characteristics.study_objective: Quantify individual-level gray matter volume (GMV) deviations with normative modeling across six psychiatric disorders and test whether heterogeneous regional deviations converge within common functional circuits and networks.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Group-based and spatial permutation tests for overlap at regional, circuit, and network levels with FDR correction; LSVM classification at chance to confirm removal of residual site effects; correlations showed scan quality (CAT12 IQR) not associated with deviation burden.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Regional GMV deviations are highly idiosyncratic (<7% regional overlap), yet converge within common circuits and networks (up to ~56% of cases), implicating salience–ventral attention and other systems transdiagnostically and by disorder.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Across 1,294 cases and 1,465 controls, regional overlap of extreme negative GMV deviations in any single parcel was <7% within diagnoses, indicating strong regional heterogeneity. Circuit-level overlap increased (up to ~40%), and network-level analyses revealed significantly greater overlap in cases versus controls across multiple systems with up to ~56% of individuals implicated, notably within salience–ventral attention transdiagnostically, and selective network involvement in MDD, BP, SCZ and ADHD. BP, MDD, OCD and SCZ exhibited greater negative deviation burden than controls, whereas ASD showed greater positive deviation burden. Findings were robust to a threshold-weighted mapping approach and validated via permutation tests.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Normative uncertainty may be higher at older ages due to younger-skewed training data; group-based parcellation choice affects overlap and may not capture individual boundaries; results depend on fixed z-threshold though a threshold-weighted approach was used for robustness; external-domain validation not reported.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Integrated HBR-based normative modeling (PCNtoolkit v0.16) with lesion network mapping using HCP rs-fMRI pipelines; used group- and spatial-permutation frameworks; mapped deviations across 1,032 parcels into canonical networks; evaluated site effects using LSVM at chance.

general_notes.general_notes: Data from 14 studies across 25 sites; QC excluded 269 scans; additional exclusion of 217 scans due to sparse site×sex HC cells; training/test split used (HCtrain ~1,196; HCtest 269). Preprocessing via CAT12/SPM12 with DARTEL. All participants aged 18–64. Representative datasets include ABIDE I/II, ASRB, FEMS, MON, IMPACT, and OpenNeuro subsets; full site/dataset details and ages are in Supplementary Table 1 and related supplementary materials. Journal confirmed as Nature Neuroscience (s41593).
